page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is a High Performance family virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. It is configured with 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading running at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and is bundled with 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 1391.28 and 2729.87 respectively, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with large block read-only speeds at 11.67 GB/sec and write speeds at 9.16 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10%. Computational benchmarks like Geekbench single-core at 982.0 and multi-core at 1733.0 further reflect its entry-level performance profile.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lower benchmark scores across database operations and Redis SET operations, this server is not designed for resource-intensive production workloads. However, the inclusion of 100 GB NVMe SSD storage alongside 4.0 GB of RAM offers a balanced resource density for low-traffic web serving, lightweight background tasks, development environments, and basic testing. It represents a cost-efficient option within the shared-resource tier for workloads that do not require sustained high-performance compute.
description: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is an entry-level virtual machine in the High Performance family, powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 2 shared vCPUs, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results indicate modest performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core scores in the bottom 25%, and memory bandwidth write speeds at 9.16 GB/sec. Database and computational operations also rank in the lower percentiles, with a Passmark database score of 496.09. Consequently, this server is best suited for lightweight, non-intensive workloads such as development environments, basic testing, and low-traffic static web serving, offering a cost-efficient entry point for shared-resource hosting.
